chapter: Baton Rouge heroes: Guy Kelly and Buddy Petit
title: Guy Kelly compared with Louis Armstrong
summary: Joe says Kelly played pretty phrases and had Louis's style but not his power or flair, and Barry notes his reputation in Celestin's band.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: I want to get into that a little later, because I know we've talked a little about you and Louis before, and I want to get into that specifically... But just sticking with Guy for the minute, some people say that Guy used a trick mouthpiece to get effects. Did you ever remember him using it?
I don't know. But coming up, I don't think Guy had the power Louis had, for one thing.
What was he most known for?

Oh, he could play pretty; I know that. He was a beautiful trumpet player. And he had a lot of things that I see in Louis...he did things in his early years... He played pretty phrases. But none of those trumpet players had that flair. Because I heard Buddy Petit... Guy Kelly was pretty young when I first heard Louis in 1912, you see. Because I came along afterwards, and in 1917, 1918, he was a pretty good trumpet player. Or in the Twenties, then he started hitting his peak; then he started playing with the top band in Baton Rouge. Like I said, I left him there.
But he never... To me at that time, he wasn't... He was just coming. He was playing good. But he had the potential...
Well, he had a great reputation with the New Orleans people that heard him.
Oh, yeah. Well, about that time... I don't know when he went to New Orleans. I know I left there in '24.
He went, I think, around '26 or something -- I think.
Well, two years could make a difference.

Because he was playing with Celestin around 1927 or '28, and you know, everybody in the Celestin band that I talked. Like, Paul Barnes was with him, and I talked to Ginnett(?) Kimball... They all say Guy Kelly was one of the best, if not the best trumpet player we had in this Celestin aggregation.
So in other words, Guy Kelly had a good local reputation, but he deserved the reputation that he got over there, he was that good, huh?

Oh, yes. To me, Guy Kelly played closer to Louis... I've got to say to you he didn't have the power and he didn't have the flair, but he had that style. Potentially, he could have been -- had he lived.
Was he influenced by Louis, or did he come up with his own style?
He was influenced by Louis. Every last one of them. He used to try to mimic Louis with his handkerchief and everything, and used to laugh at him.
